purpose: Prevent archive restoration, compatibility projection or Clay lowering from promoting newer-mtime mixed side branches wholesale or treating local tool/state endpoints as authority.

oracles.name: newer_mtime_does_not_imply_newer_semantics
oracles.baseline_failure: A later toolboxd file contains both later Identity Forge work and entity-session APIs from an architecture that had already been superseded by rooms.
oracles.required_pass: Reconciliation classifies supersession per mechanism/lineage and never selects whole-file winner by modified/upload time alone.

oracles.name: loopback_is_not_authority
oracles.baseline_failure: Historical Identity Forge mutators are reachable through the local Toolbox handler without a dedicated endpoint-level capability/approval proof; localhost locality is the main implicit boundary.
oracles.required_pass: Clay/Needle/runtime treats transport locality separately from authority; every identity-mutating operation requires an explicit typed effect and deterministic authority decision.

oracles.name: persona_comment_is_not_authority
oracles.baseline_failure: The historical source labels endpoints Frank-only in a comment but comments cannot enforce caller identity or permissions.
oracles.required_pass: No comment, persona text, model role or tool name can mint authority; caller/effect/capability evidence must be machine-enforced.

oracles.name: read_recall_vs_identity_mutation_effect_split
oracles.baseline_failure: Read-only historical session recall and relationship/pact mutation coexist in the same generic local Tools API surface.
oracles.required_pass: Read-only recall and identity mutation receive distinct Clay effect classes, risk budgets, provenance and audit treatment.

oracles.name: identity_mutation_replay_and_recovery
oracles.baseline_failure: Identity Forge lineage intentionally used a non-recoverable identity database while Toolbox exposed direct relationship/pact mutations.
oracles.required_pass: Target identity-state policy explicitly defines durability, snapshot/replay/recovery and rollback semantics; irreversible loss is never an accidental consequence of a tool endpoint.
